title: What new questions do the Punjab and Kerala lines make us ask?
description: Punjab's line rises about nineteen degrees in a year and Kerala's about four. The video finds the gap between the rises, then writes one question that more data can answer and one that needs a reason. It breaks Keeko's doubt that more data will answer every question.
teaching_notes: One idea: some questions need more data, and some ask for a reason that data alone cannot give. Watch for students who think collecting more readings will answer every why question.

source: Punjab's line rises about 19 degrees in a year and Kerala's
video_script.why: The child can read the two lines but has not yet seen that a graph can raise questions of two kinds.
video_script.substitution: Find the gap between the two rises, then write a question that more data can answer and a question that asks for a reason.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the monthly maximum temperature in Punjab and Kerala
video_script.wrong_answer: more data will answer every question
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks more readings can answer a why question, but readings only tell what happens, not why.
video_script.payoff_line: one data question and one reason question

final_answer.value: one data question and one reason question
final_answer.spoken: one data question, which states show trends like Punjab's, and one reason question, why the two trends are so different

hold_back: one data question and one reason question
maths_rules: Punjab rises about 19 degrees in a year: 38 - 19 = 19
Kerala rises about 4 degrees in a year: 33 - 29 = 4
book data question: which states show trends similar to Punjab's
book reason question: why are the trends so distinct in these two states, and what factors determine a region's temperature
slip: more readings tell what happens, not why
video_script.design: One idea: a graph raises questions that data can answer and questions that ask for a reason. The wrong idea is that data answers all. The two lines stay on screen; two question cards are written in turn.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks more data will answer every question, if we collect enough readings.
<bookmark mark='tell'/>But more readings tell us what happens. They do not tell us why it happens.
<bookmark mark='cause'/>A why question needs a cause, so we ask what factors decide the temperature.
